claims.claim_summary: Constrained compilation provides a scalable and auditable framework for benchmark creation
claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results establish constrained compilation as a scalable and auditable framework for medical VLM benchmark construction beyond question generation.

evidence_spans.source_text: In construction analysis, MedBenchAgent achieves a Task-Space F1 of 90.9%, compared with 79.2–80.0% for direct task induction and 85.1% when the same task prior is provided to the direct model.
For correctly identified tasks, 994 of 1,000 sampled items pass human audit.
The audit population comprised all 16,248 finalized items accepted by the automatic screening and audit procedures in the completed BrEaST, BUS-BRA, and VinDr-Mammo runs.

To assess the cross-domain portability of MedBenchAgent, we apply the complete construction workflow under a specialized medical setting using ISIC 2018 (Codella et al., 2019; Tschandl et al., 2018), with a distinct dataset and annotation schema.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Demonstrates domain portability and uncovers fine-grained VLM performance variations
claims.claim_text_verbatim: We further demonstrate portability to a specialized medical domain and evaluate twelve VLMs, revealing task- and setting-specific variation obscured by aggregate scores.

evidence_spans.source_text: To assess the cross-domain portability of MedBenchAgent, we apply the complete construction workflow under a specialized medical setting using ISIC 2018 (Codella et al., 2019; Tschandl et al., 2018), with a distinct dataset and annotation schema.
We evaluate twelve VLMs spanning general-purpose and medical-domain model families, multiple parameter scales, and different inference regimes.

To quantify such changes, we compare all 66 model pairs and find that 12–24 pairs (18.2–36.4%) reverse ordering between Overall Acc. and individual-task Acc.; within tasks, 4–15 pairs (6.1–22.7%) reverse between Acc. and F1.
